newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy Feb CPI seen at -0.1 pct m/m after 11 cities.
newsitem.headline: Italy Feb CPI seen at -0.1 pct m/m after 11 cities.

text.p: Italy's inflation rate is estimated to be -0.1 percent month-on-month and 2.2 year-on-year in February, according to economists' forecasts based on consumer prices data from 11 sample Italian cities.
Final CPI was 0.2 percent month-on-month in January and 2.6 percent year-on-year. Analysts had forecast February CPI at 0.2 percent on a monthly basis and 2.5 percent on a yearly basis.
Final February figures are due on March 4 and together all 11 cities have a weighting of 75.66 percent on the national index.
The 2.2 percent rate, if confirmed by final data, will be Italy's lowest level of inflation since May 1969.
However economists took note of a decision by an Italian administrative court on Friday to suspend recently introduced cuts in electricity tariffs charged by state-owned utility Enel until April 4.
The decision overrides cuts introduced on February 13 and an electricity industry source said old tariffs will be introduced from Friday until April 4 when the matter will be decided.
Ilaria Fornari, economist at JP Morgan here, said the tariff cut had contributed a 0.14 percentage point fall in the year-on-year inflation rate this month.
Taken out of the equation, she said preliminary data would have shown inflation at some 2.4 percent year-on-year in February against 2.2 percent.
However, other analysts said the tariff change was unlikely to show an effect on prices until March.
Robert Prior, European economist at HSBC Markets in London, said the tariff decision meant there might be a revision to the figure when the final rate is published on March 4.
If so, that meant the final figure might be more like 0.1 rather than -0.1 percent on a monthly basis and 2.4 rather than 2.2 percent.
"But it's still a pretty good number," Prior said, adding he would expect a cut of 75 basis points in the 6.75 percent discount rate over the next two to three months.
"The Bank of Italy may wait until the mini-budget is out of the way but inflation remains firmly under control partly reflecting weakness of activity at the moment," he said.
The government has said it intends to carry out additional budget measures to pare Italy's budget deficit this year. Details of the measures will be announced in coming weeks.
